evidence.quote: To get a list of users in an organization, use

assumptions: The source does not list the organization-wide user listing endpoint. It only points to 'Users: getUsers'. I assumed it is GET /v2/organizations/{organizationId}/users. Please verify this path.
Paging for that user list (start/take, page size 100, total in paging.total_set_size) is copied from the group listing endpoint and not confirmed for users.
The user field names (id, email, user_name, user_status, last_login, created_on) come from the user profile responses and may differ in the user list response.
The user_status values (active, closed, activationrequired, activationsent, disabled) are guesses, because the source does not list them.
The source gives the same URL for authorize and token. The token URL is normally a separate endpoint, so please confirm it.
The docs say user authentication is needed, so an application token (such as a service account) will not work. The connection will stop working if the authorizing person leaves.
The first organization returned is assumed to be the one to read.
No rate limits are stated in the source.
User type and role are not mapped because no clear field was found.

findings.message: Docs are on docusign.com but the connector calls api.docusign.net. Confirm this is the vendor's own domain, because credentials will be sent there.
"last_login" is not in the response schema.
Pagination has no supporting quote from the source.
The source gives no rate limit, so the connector relies on backoff alone.
The source does not list the organization-wide user listing endpoint. It only points to 'Users: getUsers'. I assumed it is GET /v2/organizations/{organizationId}/users. Please verify this path.
